messages:
deploy-bot: Deploy blocked — production deploy for tag v2.8.0-rc3 is held by CI gate. Failing jobs: smoke-tests, integration-db-migrations. Commit: 9f3b2a1. Triggered by: @Beth R. CI: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/7777 :warning:
Alex H: which jobs exactly are failing? smoke vs full-integration?
CI System: smoke-tests (job 7777-smoke) failed: 1/12 tests. integration-db-migrations (job 7777-db) failed: migration_apply error. Logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/7777/logs
Maria C: putting the failing tail here, looks like the migration step throws a duplicate key on users.email after seeding:
```
  ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "users_email_key"
  at org.postgres.Driver.execute(…)
  SQL: INSERT INTO users(email, ... ) values ( 'ci_user@example.com', ... )
```
Samir K: hmm that specific duplication has been flaky in sandbox lately — seeds reuse the same test email sometimes. Could be a flaky test rather than a real migration bug.
Beth R: if it's just seed collision we could re-run CI and proceed with the canary, but the db migration job touches prod schemas (adding column users.flags). I don't want to risk a half-applied migration. Need a clear owner to confirm.
Alex H: I can triage the migration job now. If it's only test data, we can re-run the migration job with a clean DB. Samir — can you trigger a rerun of the failing jobs?
Samir K: re-run queued for smoke-tests and integration-db-migrations (jobs 7777-smoke, 7777-db). cc @deploy-bot :rocket:
deploy-bot: Re-run requested by Samir K. Status: queued.
CI System: job 7777-smoke re-run started. job 7777-db re-run started.
CI System: job 7777-smoke passed on re-run.
CI System: job 7777-db re-run failed again — same duplicate key on users.email. Full log: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/7777/retry/logs
Maria C: looks deterministic now — the migration script calls a seed helper that inserts a fixture user without checking uniqueness. This would fail on prod if the migration ran after users were created. We need a migration fix (add ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING or guard) or to revert the migration. PR #4521 touched this area.
Samir K: quick options: 1) Pin deploy to v2.8.0-rc2 (previous tag) and un-block, 2) Patch migration in PR and block until green, 3) Force skip migration step (risky).
Beth R: pinning to rc2 might be safest for today to keep the release train moving — but confirm there are no security fixes in rc3 we need. Alex H, can you verify rc2 -> production delta? If safe, we'll pin and reschedule rc3 hotfix.
Alex H: checking changelog/commits now. I see one non-critical UI fix and two perf tweaks in rc3; no security patches. I can create a pinned release for rc2 and re-trigger.
deploy-bot: Action required: release-manager approval to pin to tag v2.8.0-rc2. React with :thumbsup: to approve or reply with objections.
Beth R: :thumbsup: — approve pin to rc2 and push release window change (moving rc3 hotfix to next business day).
Maria C: leaving a note — we'll open PR to fix migration (add uniqueness guard) and run a db-migration-focused test against a copy of prod data before reattempt.
Samir K: I'll re-run the deploy pipeline pinned to rc2 once deploy-bot receives approval.
deploy-bot: Deploy pinned to v2.8.0-rc2 on hold until pipeline re-run. Status: blocked -> awaiting pipeline run.
Beth R: moving out of today's change window. Creating follow-up ticket: RELEASE-1243 to track migration fix + verification. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
